name: Feberis Pro
one_line: Flipper Zero add-on module adding RF/SubGHz, WiFi, BLE and GPS radios beyond the Flipper's stock hardware; USD price as shown on lab401.com's US store.
why_notable: Combines several wireless attack radios (RF, WiFi, BLE, GPS) into one Flipper Zero expansion board, claimed 10x over stock Flipper radio performance.

name: AWOK Dual C5 Touch
one_line: Touchscreen Flipper Zero wardriving add-on with dual-band (2.4/5GHz) WiFi 6 and BLE radios for wireless auditing.
why_notable: May be a newer WiFi6/C5-chipset generation of the AWOK Dual Touch v3 already tracked; flagged for reviewer comparison rather than silently dropped.

name: DigiLab for FlipperZero
one_line: Flipper Zero module for probing digital electronics: measures voltages, observes logic signals and reads sensor/module protocols on target hardware.
why_notable: Turns the Flipper Zero into a basic bench probe for voltage, logic-signal and protocol inspection during hardware audits.

name: MastaBlasta - IR Blaster
one_line: Long-range infrared blaster add-on for Flipper Zero that boosts IR transmit distance/power for remote-control attacks.
why_notable: Higher-power active IR transmitter module for Flipper Zero IR replay attacks, beyond the stock IR emitter's range.

name: IR Blaster
one_line: Seven-LED infrared blaster add-on for Flipper Zero that boosts IR transmit range/power for remote-control attacks.
why_notable: Base-tier active IR transmitter expansion for Flipper Zero IR attacks, a lower-cost sibling to the MastaBlasta/Slim Shady IR blasters.

name: USB RFID Reader/Writer DL533N
one_line: USB-stick 13.56MHz LibNFC-compatible reader/writer that reads, writes, dumps and emulates MIFARE/NFC HF cards from a PC.
why_notable: Low-cost USB-tethered HF RFID read/write/crack tool, a different form factor from standalone devices like the Proxmark or ACR122U.

name: RFID Field Detector Ultra - LF/HF/UHF
one_line: Passive, battery-free tri-band (LF/HF/UHF) detector that lights up to indicate the presence of an active RFID reader field.
why_notable: Covers all three RFID frequency bands in one passive field-presence detector, useful for locating hidden readers during a physical audit.

name: Stealth Decoy Reader
one_line: Rapidly-deployed decoy RFID/PIN-pad reader that captures badge and PIN credentials to a phone app, with optional wireless relay to a Proxmark for cloning.
why_notable: Purpose-built credential-harvesting decoy reader distinct from long-range skimmers, aimed specifically at capturing card+PIN combos.

name: Long-range iCLASS RFID Capture System
one_line: Long-range (seller states up to ~45cm) covert HF skimmer for iCLASS badges, phone-managed with optional wireless relay to a Proxmark for cloning.
why_notable: Purpose-built long-range skimmer for the iCLASS badge format, well beyond typical proximity-card read range.

name: Long-range MaxiProx 5375 125KHz Capture System
one_line: Long-range (seller states up to ~60cm) covert 125kHz LF skimmer built on the HID MaxiProx 5375 reader, phone-managed with optional Proxmark relay for cloning.
why_notable: Long-range LF badge skimmer offering roughly double the capture distance of typical HF long-range readers in this catalog.

name: Dual Mode Paxton Long Range / Stealth Decoy Reader
one_line: Combined long-range skimmer and decoy reader specifically for Paxton access-control badges, phone-managed with optional Proxmark relay.
why_notable: Seller states this is the first dedicated long-range skimmer/decoy built specifically for the Paxton badge ecosystem.

name: Long Range RFID Reader/Writer DL533N XL
one_line: Long-range (up to 18cm) LibNFC-compatible USB reader/writer for ISO14443A/B (MIFARE Classic/Ultralight/DESFire/FeliCa/NTAG) cards, meant to be hidden under furniture or in a bag.
why_notable: Long-range variant of the DL533N USB reader/writer, extending covert read/write/sniff range to 18cm versus a few cm on the standard model.

name: UHFKill
one_line: Handheld tool that wirelessly and permanently disables UHF RFID tags embedded in clothing, shoes and retail products.
why_notable: The only dedicated UHF tag-deactivation tool in the catalog, distinct from the several HF/LF-focused NFC-kill devices already tracked.

name: 13.56MHz RFID Field Strength Meter
one_line: Passive, ISO-calibrated meter that gives a quantitative 13.56MHz RFID field-strength reading rather than a simple presence indicator.
why_notable: Calibrated measurement tool (vs. simple pass/fail detectors) for verifying HF reader field strength during compliance or audit work.

name: Proxmark 3 RDV4 - BlueShark Standalone Module
one_line: Drop-in Bluetooth + battery module that lets a Proxmark 3 RDV4 run standalone scripts without a host computer.
why_notable: Adds untethered/wireless standalone operation to the Proxmark 3 RDV4, a genuine capability change rather than a passive accessory.

name: iCS Decoder for iCLASS SE / SEOS Decoder
one_line: Plug-in decoder module for the iCopy-X that decodes and clones iCLASS SE and iCLASS SEOS badges.
why_notable: Seller states this is the only device able to clone iCLASS SE/SEOS badges, a higher-security HID format most cloners cannot touch.

name: Chameleon Lite
one_line: Low-cost RFID emulator specialised in HF/MIFARE emulation, positioned below the Chameleon Ultra/Tiny in the same product family.
why_notable: Entry-level Chameleon-series emulator; capability may overlap with the Chameleon Tiny already tracked, included for reviewer comparison.

name: Industrial Handheld UHF Reader
one_line: Industrial handheld UHF RFID reader used alongside UHFKill to locate embedded tags and confirm they were deactivated, including full carton sweeps.
why_notable: High-end companion reader for the UHFKill deactivation workflow, filling a tag-location/verification role no other catalog item covers.

name: Proxmark 5 - Wireless + Battery Module
one_line: Drop-in wireless + battery module that lets a Proxmark 5 run mobile/untethered for field pentests.
why_notable: Adds standalone wireless operation to the Proxmark 5, mirroring the BlueShark module's role for the Proxmark 3.

name: ARD RFID Blocker (Pack of 2) - NFC Blocker
one_line: Credit-card-sized, battery-free active RFID/NFC jammer that blocks reads of cards placed above or below it, unlike passive faraday-sleeve wallets.
why_notable: Active jamming device rather than a passive shield, a distinct defensive capability from typical RFID-blocking wallets/sleeves.

name: MACOBOX - Hardware Pentest Platform
one_line: All-in-one hardware pentesting platform for rapid connection, firmware dumping and analysis across multiple hardware interfaces.
why_notable: Top-end (~$11k) integrated hardware-hacking lab-in-a-box, the highest-priced item in the catalog and a distinct product tier from single-purpose tools like Bus Pirate or GreatFET.

name: O.MG Malicious Cable Detector
one_line: USB inline device that uses side-channel power analysis (200,000 samples/sec) to detect known malicious USB cables, and doubles as a USB data blocker (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Defensive counterpart to O.MG-style malicious cables already tracked; no comparable detection device is currently in the database.

name: PiKVM v4 Plus
one_line: Hardware KVM-over-IP remote access unit with a built-in 3/4/5G modem, marketed by the seller as an undetectable remote-access tool for red-team engagements (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Cellular-connected out-of-band remote access hardware, a distinct implant category from the USB/network-tap tools already tracked.

name: Alfa AWUS036ACHM
one_line: High-gain USB WiFi adapter with a monitor-mode/packet-injection-capable chipset, sold specifically for wireless auditing (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Standard high-sensitivity monitor-mode/injection WiFi adapter used alongside tools like the WiFi Pineapple for wardriving and deauth/capture work.

name: TermDriver 2
one_line: USB-to-serial adapter with an onboard screen that shows live serial traffic for debugging and monitoring headless/embedded systems.
why_notable: Serial debug adapter with an integrated display, filling a niche between a bare USB-UART cable and a full logic analyzer.

name: BugBlat miniSniffer 2
one_line: Compact, cross-platform USB protocol analyzer/sniffer for capturing and inspecting USB device traffic (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Dedicated low-cost USB bus analyzer, filling a gap between Cynthion-class USB reverse-engineering tools and basic sniffers.

name: I2CDriver
one_line: Dedicated I2C bus development/debug tool with an onboard screen showing live bus activity for flashing and testing I2C devices.
why_notable: Single-protocol I2C debug probe with a live display, a narrower/cheaper alternative to multi-protocol tools like the Bus Pirate.

name: SPIDriver
one_line: Dedicated SPI bus development/debug tool with an onboard screen, the SPI-protocol sibling to the I2CDriver (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Single-protocol SPI debug probe with live display, fills the same niche as I2CDriver but for SPI devices.

name: CANBus Module for Flipper Zero
one_line: Flipper Zero add-on board that connects to a vehicle's CAN bus / OBD-II port for development, debugging and diagnostics (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: The catalog's only dedicated automotive CAN-bus interface, extending the Flipper Zero into vehicle diagnostics/analysis.

name: Minino: IoT Multitool
one_line: Standalone handheld multitool that detects, sniffs and manipulates BLE, Zigbee, Thread, Matter and other IoT/sub-GHz protocols.
why_notable: Seller-described first dedicated multi-protocol IoT sniffing/manipulation tool, covering Zigbee/Thread/Matter which no other catalog device targets directly.

name: TinySA Ultra+
one_line: Handheld spectrum analyzer for identifying and locating RF-transmitting devices across its supported frequency range.
why_notable: General-purpose spectrum analyzer used across SDR, IoT and RF audits to visually confirm transmissions the other capture tools decode.

name: Kronos Electric Pick
one_line: Motorized electric pick gun with adjustable strike amplitude for opening pin-tumbler locks, including higher-security cylinders.
why_notable: The only powered/electronic lock-opening tool in the physical-audit lineup; the rest of that category is purely mechanical picks and bypass tools.

name: Project Reboot: Hardware Audit Training Target
one_line: Deliberately vulnerable practice target with progressive UART, SPI, I2C and Bluetooth challenges for learning hardware-hacking techniques (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: A training target (not an attack tool itself) built specifically to practice the same interfaces (UART/SPI/I2C/BLE) that tools like the Bus Pirate attack.

name: Lab401 Flashing Multi-tool for Proxmark & Chameleon
one_line: Small dongle for quickly reflashing/recovering Proxmark and Chameleon RFID devices (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Purpose-built recovery/flashing tool for two device families already tracked; marginal but distinct utility.

name: Glytch GPS Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: GPS add-on module for the WiFi Pineapple Pager that geotags captured networks/clients for wardriving (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Adds location-tagging to WiFi Pineapple Pager wardriving sessions, a real functional addition rather than a passive accessory.

name: Glytch Mesh Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: LoRa mesh-networking add-on for the WiFi Pineapple Pager enabling decentralized, off-grid messaging between units (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Gives the WiFi Pineapple Pager a sub-GHz LoRa mesh comms channel independent of WiFi/cellular infrastructure.

name: Glytch Ethernet Module for Pineapple Pager
one_line: Wired Ethernet add-on for the WiFi Pineapple Pager enabling LAN-based payload deployment in addition to its WiFi radios (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: Turns the WiFi-only Pineapple Pager into a wired network implant as well, similar in role to a LAN Turtle.

name: Opera Cake for HackRF
one_line: Antenna-switching expansion board for a HackRF One that automatically selects among up to 8 external antennas or 4 filters (price converted from EUR).
why_notable: RF front-end switching accessory that adds automated multi-antenna/filter operation to an existing HackRF One, though it has no function without one.

name: NanoVNA-F
one_line: Handheld vector network analyzer for measuring and tuning antennas across SDR/RF setups.
why_notable: Common companion tool for tuning antennas on SDR and RF security-testing rigs; borderline since it's a general RF measurement instrument rather than an attack tool.

name: ChipWhisperer - HuskyPlus
one_line: Side-channel power analysis and fault-injection platform; appears to be an enhanced-FPGA version of the ChipWhisperer Husky already tracked.
why_notable: May simply be a larger-FPGA SKU of the ChipWhisperer-Husky already in the database; flagged for reviewer comparison rather than silently dropped.
